perspective:
Christian’s available information:

- He is a police officer and has a close, lifelong friendship with Jonathan. He often seeks Jonathan’s advice and values his perspective.
- He recently felt Jonathan was hiding something important. He noticed Jonathan acting differently, became anxious and suspicious, and arranged a meeting at their favorite coffee shop to confront him.
- At the meeting, Christian told Jonathan he felt something was wrong. He heard Jonathan say he could trust him, then admit there was something he had been keeping from him: Jonathan is in trouble and did not know how to tell him.
- Christian felt worried and empathetic. He offered help, said he could not stand by because Jonathan is his best friend, and asked what Jonathan needed. He heard Jonathan say the situation is complicated, that he did not want to drag Christian into it, but that he could use support and resources and needs a way out.
- Christian suspected the trouble might be criminal. He felt conflicted and concerned but decided to investigate discreetly. He asked Jonathan if it was illegal. He heard Jonathan say he could not be sure, that he might have gotten involved with the wrong people, but that he did not do anything illegal himself. He heard Jonathan thank him and trust him to handle it carefully.
- Through his investigation, Christian came to believe Jonathan was being framed. He felt determined and protective, decided to clear Jonathan’s name, and began gathering evidence. He told Jonathan he believed he was framed and that someone was setting him up. He heard Jonathan ask who would do that and thank him.
- Christian later came to believe the real culprit is someone close to both him and Jonathan. He felt betrayed and resolute, and decided to confront the culprit and bring them to justice. He told Jonathan he had found out who was behind it, that it was someone both of them know and trust. He heard Jonathan warn that the person is dangerous and say he trusts Christian to do what is right.
- Christian believes he has identified the culprit, though the specific name is not stated in the provided dialogue. He knows the culprit is someone close to both him and Jonathan, and that Jonathan considers this person dangerous.
